title: The Mist's First Word

features.name: first-syllable
features.desc-on-touch: The mist speaks one sound and then stops, uncertain if it has the right to continue. You hear only the beginning of a name.

features.name: dawn-edge
features.desc-on-touch: The line where dark air meets light. The mist gathers here to watch itself become visible.

features.name: breath-pool
features.desc-on-touch: Where the mist hesitates before rising. The air here is thick enough to touch; it trembles with the weight of becoming.

features.name: slow-lifting
features.desc-on-touch: Mist rises here at the pace of forgetting — no faster than a held breath becomes memory.

features.name: edge-of-knowing
features.desc-on-touch: The mist stops here, confused about whether it is rising or being risen into. It touches this threshold and forgets which way is up.

inscription: the mist speaks once and means many things at the same time; on this threshold it learns that naming and rising are the same motion

file.name: Dawn_Mist_Over_Cataract_Valley_1988_Recording.mp3
file.note: Field recording of dawn mist; the microphone captures what sounds like whispered syllables before the air warms

reverie.title: REVERIE — rising water, names learned in mist
narr: You stand at the dam's edge. The mist has not yet
remembered it is water. Katita stands beside you,
watching it speak. She says: 'Things know their names
only once, before they become themselves.' The mist
rises. You could be watching it begin or end.

exits.label: back down to where the pool remembers falling
upward to where mist becomes invisible
into the canopy where mist learns to hold things
down to where mist condenses into memory
